01.r: Opens the first limit on the king.
01.n: The Hebrew is 'and not', a flat negation of the kind used for lasting prohibitions; it is counted here with the verb it negates.

02.r: He must not keep adding wives.
02.n: The verb means to be or become many; in this causative form, to make many. BDB: be, or become, much, many, great.

04.r: Wives taken into the king's house.
04.n: The ordinary word for woman, here in the sense wife; Gesenius notes this plural form, always used for the plural.

05.r: Gives what the first limit guards against.
05.n: Again 'and not'. The clause states the danger the law guards against, so the Geneva and BSB say 'lest' and the KJV 'that ... not'.

06.r: His heart would be drawn away from the LORD.
06.n: Gesenius gives the first sense as to turn aside, to depart, and notes the special sense 'to depart from God', to turn away from his worship. That this is the danger here is a reasonable reading of the verse; it names no object.

07.r: The king's inner self: his mind and will.
07.n: BDB: inner man, mind, will, heart. The DRC says 'his mind'.

08.n: Gesenius: silver, so called from its pale colour; BDB lists silver as wealth. The same word is used of silver as money; our register renders it 'silver' throughout.

09.n: BDB lists gold as wealth and as spoil of war among its senses.

10.r: The second limit, as flat as the first.

11.r: He must not heap up silver and gold.
11.n: The same verb as the one that limits his wives, so the two limits are worded alike.

13.r: The limit is on great amounts, not on owning any silver or gold.
13.n: Gesenius gives the word first as a noun, strength, force, and then as an adverb, very, exceedingly. It stands last in the verse, so the limit falls on the amount; that the king may keep some is a reasonable reading, not something the verse says outright.

06.n: μεταστήσεται is a future of μεθίστημι, to remove, change over; the brief gives no dictionary form.

08.n: ἀργύριον, silver, and silver money: the word our register renders 'silver' in the Gospels.
